column3: NASB follows the critical text, supplying “covenant” where the Textus Receptus has “tabernacle.”
“The first room” is rendered “the outer one,” and “the presentation of the bread” “the sacred bread.”
Close to the Greek.
“Covered around in every part” is rendered “covered on all sides,” and “tablets” “tables.”
“Not it is now the time to speak” is rendered “we cannot now speak.”
“The first” is rendered “the outer,” and “at all times” “continually.”
NASB supplies “taking” and “committed.”
“The first tabernacle” is rendered “the outer tabernacle,” and “made manifest” “disclosed.”
NASB begins a new sentence with “Accordingly.”
NASB follows the critical text (“regulations for the body,” without “and”); “flesh” is rendered “body.”
NASB reads “to come” with the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “that have come.” NASB supplies “He entered.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
NASB reads “your conscience” with the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “our.” “Unblemished” is rendered “without blemish.”
NASB supplies “that were committed.”
“Will” is rendered “covenant”; the Greek word means both.
“A will” is rendered “a covenant,” and “after death” “only when men are dead.”
NASB supplies “covenant.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Law,” “and the goats”).
The quotation is in capitals.
Close to the Greek.
“Almost” is rendered “one may almost say.”
“Representations” is rendered “copies.”
NASB adds “mere.”
“Repeatedly” is rendered “often,” and “with the blood of another” “with blood not his own.”
NASB follows the critical text (“sin”); “has been revealed” is rendered “has been manifested.”
NASB supplies “comes.”
“Apart from sin” is rendered “without reference to sin.”
